issues.title: [F01] Alternative names (aliases and redirects)
issues.body:
**Original point:** LLM to generate appropriate alternative names for an article that someone might look up a certain thing by description.

**Interpretation:** Wikipedia-style redirects. The LLM proposes 3-8 aliases per page; code identifiers owned by the feature (HTTP routes, table names, env vars, CLI commands) are added deterministically. Aliases feed search and redirect URLs, and a rename appends the old title.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #1 (core engine). Spec section 3 and 7.3.

issues.title: [F02] Hyperlinks to related pages
issues.body:
**Original point:** Hyperlinks to related pages.

**Interpretation:** Links in the body text on first mention, restricted to manifest IDs and aliases; unknown targets render as plain text. See also lists the top 5 graph neighbours.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #1. Spec section 7.3.

issues.title: [F03] Works cited with code lines
issues.body:
**Original point:** Works cited at bottom with codebase lines.

**Interpretation:** Numbered References rendered from claim citations as path:Lstart-Lend@sha permalinks. Each code citation stores a contentHash of the cited lines, which makes citations the staleness detector.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #1. Spec sections 5 and 6.

issues.title: [F04] Pages by feature, not folder
issues.body:
**Original point:** LLM generated pages based by feature rather than folder in the codebase.

**Interpretation:** Features come from clustering a weighted import + co-change graph; the LLM names, merges, and splits clusters into a manifest with permanent IDs.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #1. ADR-0001.

issues.title: [F05] Generated from each PR
issues.body:
**Original point:** Autogenerated based on a PR.

**Interpretation:** `repowiki update` processes new commits and rewrites only stale sections; `replay` walks first-parent merge commits. Local trigger in v1, a GitHub Action later.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #2. Spec section 6.

issues.title: [F06] Versioned, dated pages
issues.body:
**Original point:** Pages versioned and dated.

**Interpretation:** Every page revision stores its commit date, sha, and PR number; the reader shows View history with diffs.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #2. Spec section 5.

issues.title: [F07] Ways an LLM can use the site
issues.body:
**Original point:** List of ways that an LLM can use the site.

**Interpretation:** v1 ships llms.txt and a JSON export, consumed by the eval agent. A full MCP server is sub-project #5.

**Verdict:** v1 (partial); remainder in sub-project #5.

issues.title: [F08] LLM reads past versions of the wiki
issues.body:
**Original point:** Looking at the dated past versions of the wiki to figure out past ideas and ways the codebase worked previously.

**Interpretation:** History queries (how did X work on date D) over stored revisions, exposed to agents.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #5. Enabled by the v1 revision store.

issues.title: [F09] Ask-me-anything sidebar that links to pages
issues.body:
**Original point:** A sidebar ask-me-anything LLM that already has the live context precomputed and can link the user to a page instead of answering everything in the chat box.

**Interpretation:** Retrieval over precomputed pages; answers are a short reply plus links to the pages that hold the detail.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #4.

issues.title: [F10] Autogenerated diagrams
issues.body:
**Original point:** Autogenerated diagrams and pictures to aid the reader, think Wikipedia.

**Interpretation:** Mermaid flowcharts built from real import and call edges (at most 12 nodes, every node verified and clickable), plus a feature map on the Main Page.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #3. Spec section 7.3.

issues.title: [F11] Pictures (UI screenshots)
issues.body:
**Original point:** Autogenerated diagrams and pictures to aid the reader.

**Interpretation:** Reshaped: screenshots of rendered UI for frontend features.

**Verdict:** later, sub-project #3.

issues.title: [F12] Addictive, Wikipedia-style browsing
issues.body:
**Original point:** A mini Wikipedia for any codebase that is engaging and has the addiction aspect Wikipedia has.

**Interpretation:** Hover previews, dense first-mention linking, Random article, Did you know (hook claims), a featured article, and recently updated pages. Judged by the rabbit-hole exit criterion.

**Verdict:** v1 (partial), sub-project #3.

issues.title: [F13] Links to real Wikipedia
issues.body:
**Original point:** Links to outside real Wikipedia pages to make browsing fun, for example explaining an algorithm or a codebase precedent.

**Interpretation:** `[[wp:Title]]` links suggested by the LLM and verified against the Wikipedia REST API, whose summary doubles as the hover preview.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #3. Spec section 7.3.

issues.title: [F14] People pages
issues.body:
**Original point:** People pages for contributors, each writing about when and where they contributed as if documenting a war, with hyperlinks to features and teammates.

**Interpretation:** A dated narrative per contributor linking to the features they shaped. In a company setting this needs opt-out from day one.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #6.

issues.title: [F15] Contribution graphs over time
issues.body:
**Original point:** Contribution graphs over time, for the whole repo and zoomable to one person.

**Interpretation:** Activity over time for the whole repo and per person, with zoom.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #6.

issues.title: [F16] Contributor identity merge
issues.body:
**Original point:** (derived during design)

**Interpretation:** Merge author identities (for example seanpatrickmay and Sean May) via a mailmap before attributing anything.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #6.

issues.title: [F17] Attribution: as-is vs full history
issues.body:
**Original point:** Generate as-is (can miss refactors; copy-pasted files misattribute authorship) or with full history (requires regeneration at each timestep, expensive).

**Interpretation:** Resolved by splitting the problem: line authorship uses git blame -C -C -M, which follows copies and moves; article history comes from replaying merges, so full history costs incremental-update tokens rather than one regeneration per point in time.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #2.

issues.title: [F18] Human edits to the wiki
issues.body:
**Original point:** Should users edit the wiki? Can edits be overwritten? Maybe the LLM figures out accuracy and corrects the generator.

**Interpretation:** No edits in v1. Later, edits become generator guidance verified against the code instead of overwriting generated text. Open question.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #7.

issues.title: [F19] Hygiene good enough to run RepoWiki on itself
issues.body:
**Original point:** Follow extremely well-groomed hygiene programming protocols so the tool can be used on its own repository.

**Interpretation:** Tiny PRs, a commit per green TDD step, merge commits, CI on every PR, and ADRs for decisions, so RepoWiki's own history is a realistic test subject.

**Verdict:** adopted from M0. CLAUDE.md and ADR-0002.

issues.title: [F20] Opinionated articles and an opinion setting
issues.body:
**Original point:** Can the articles be opinionated? Can there be a setting to change the opinion?

**Interpretation:** Reshaped: NPOV voice; opinions appear only as evidence-backed Known limitations claims. The opinion setting is deferred to sub-project #7.

**Verdict:** v1 (NPOV); setting in v2.

issues.title: [F21] Voice learned from Wikipedia
issues.body:
**Original point:** How do we make the voice correct? Try to learn this from Wikipedia itself.

**Interpretation:** A checked-in style guide distilled from Wikipedia's Manual of Style: a bold-subject first sentence, a standalone lead, NPOV, verifiability, no original research, and words to avoid.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #1. Spec section 7.1.

issues.title: [F22] Wikis for every repo in a company
issues.body:
**Original point:** A wiki for all codebases in the company, easily accessible, so you can work off another team's code.

**Interpretation:** A multi-repo index with cross-repo links.

**Verdict:** v3, sub-project #8.

issues.title: [F23] Pages for future changes, issues, and PRs
issues.body:
**Original point:** Is there a way to have a page for future changes? Issues? PRs?

**Interpretation:** In-progress pages built from open issues and PRs, linked to the features they touch. RepoWiki's own tracker is the first test data.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #9.

issues.title: [F24] Opinion and rebuttal loop with coding agents
issues.body:
**Original point:** The LLM takes an opinion when writing; the LLM changing that code can either act on it or write a rebuttal to the article creator. Limit how extreme opinions can be; report design choices factually.

**Interpretation:** v1 caps extremity structurally: a limitation claim cannot exist without cited evidence. The rebuttal channel is sub-project #7.

**Verdict:** v2, sub-project #7.

issues.title: [F25] Token savings vs reading the codebase
issues.body:
**Original point:** (derived during design) It is precomputed once, so it saves token usage massively compared with every engineer's agent reading the whole codebase.

**Interpretation:** Every LLM call is logged in a token ledger; the Q&A eval compares wiki-only and repo-only agents on accuracy and tokens and reports the break-even point.

**Verdict:** v1, measured. Spec section 9.

issues.title: [F26] Stable page identity
issues.body:
**Original point:** (derived during design)

**Interpretation:** Feature IDs are permanent slugs; merges become redirects and splits become disambiguation pages, so URLs and history never break.

**Verdict:** v1, sub-project #1. Spec section 5.
